statement: On 200 held-out Simple English Wikipedia questions (the knowledge bar's own draw, first sentences hidden from the ingest) and 200 algebra and sequence questions, the ask path of act/prompt.mjs was run on one bare brain with the knowledge tier on and off, interleaved per question, the model cell on provider null. With the tier on, 176 of 200 wiki questions (88.0%) were answered natively, without reaching a model cell, against 0 (0.0%) with it off; wiki accuracy was 61.0% on and 0.0% off, the native answers took a mean 5736.8 microseconds, and the model cell was called 24 times on and 200 off. On the suite the tier changed nothing it could: accuracy 100.0% on and 100.0% off, 200 and 200 native, 0 and 0 model calls. The confidence floor was 0.2, chosen on the 428 held-out records outside this draw. 0 hidden sentences were found in the store. The bar is met. Contaminated: the wiki draw (seed knowledge-draw-2026-09-23) is the one bench/verdicts/knowledge.json grades, so its results were on disk while this tier was developed.

development.what: the confidence floor chosen by --tune on the held-out records OUTSIDE the bar's draw; the bench/answer.mjs algebra and sequence suites

heldOut.what: the wiki questions: bench/knowledge.mjs drawHeldout (its DRAW_SEED), first sentences hidden from the ingest; the suite questions are a no-regression check with no held-out set

split.contaminated: the wiki draw (seed knowledge-draw-2026-09-23) is the one bench/verdicts/knowledge.json grades, so its results were on disk while this tier was developed

bar: the native share on the wiki questions rises with the tier on, and the suite accuracy does not fall

config.interleaved: even questions tier on first, odd questions tier off first

definitions.native: the model cell was never reached: provenance.llm.provider is null (an exact answer, or the knowledge tier at or above its floor)
definitions.accuracyWiki: the hidden first sentence head noun (plural folded) among the words of the answer line read by bench/answer.mjs extractAnswer; an answer beginning "nothing in memory matches" is an abstention and wrong
definitions.nativeMeanUs: mean wall time of the whole ask() call, in microseconds, over the native answers
definitions.modelCalls: answers whose provenance.llm.provider is not null: askModel was called
